There's a massive amount of two problems here: 1) Ignorance of how DNA testing actually works, and 2) Inability to actually read the article.

First, the article plainly states that while the results are not identical, they are largely the same for all companies.

Second, the 99.6% similarity, while interesting, is not the most likely primary source of the discrepancies. This would actually be the result of "no-calls" in the individual tests; spots on the DNA where the test could not get a good enough read to give a result. Even you taking the test multiple times would result in different no-calls each time, to the point where your own results would vary slightly because each test would be missing hundreds or even thousands of spots out of the ~700,000 spots out of your 3.2 BILLION base pairs that are actually tested.

And if you're missing spots that are key to establishing a particular ancestral bit of DNA, then that's going to affect your results because the algorithm doesn't have the same data to work with. Largely the same, but importantly different due to these missing data points. Enough to make the results very similar, but still not perfectly identical.

Is there anything about this you folks don't understand?

Here's an actual example from my actual data.

The raw data results file is 701,478 lines long (excluding header description and comments.)

13,616 of those results are "no-calls".

That means that almost 2% of my results were "no-calls", where the test did not return results for thousands of different base pairs of my DNA.

Now compare that to my buddy, who has 19,923 "no-calls" in his results. That's almost three percent of his raw data that is missing.

Now even if he and I were identical twins, how much variance in our ethnicity do you expect there to be when a few percent of our results are missing right out of the gate? So we're not actually comparing identical DNA, but only mostly identical DNA.

This article is sadly ignorant fear mongering. The people involved in it should have known better.

But even more so, the people commenting here should know better because the article itself makes it very clear that the results are still mostly identical and even gave some reasons for why they might vary, even though they didn't explain the actual elephant in the room and primary reason, which anyone with a reasonable knowledge of how DNA testing actually works SHOULD KNOW.
